cells.tense: You're here with the pen in your hand, keeping the level between what you give and what you take, and it's on purpose.
cells.ask: Name one thing someone gave you recently that you haven't let yourself count, and count it out loud today.
cells.core: Around you the exchange runs clean. Someone brings something, you put something back, and nobody keeps a tab, because the fairness is steady enough to trust without watching it. It shows in who calls you first and what they bring when they do, and in how easy it is for people to lean on you without flinching. You're becoming what you are in this: the level you keep isn't a rule you follow, it's how you show up, and people feel it in the room the way you'd feel a chair pulled out for you. What that gives back is a room where nobody has to be careful with you.
cells.sheetLine: The fairness in the room is part of how you're made, and you're the one holding it.
cells.verb: fair exchange — giving and receiving kept level between people
cells.place: becoming what you are, letting what's yours show without shrinking or dressing it up

cells.tense: You're already at the end of an exchange that hasn't happened, squaring the books before anyone has spoken.
cells.ask: Pick the unfinished exchange you're most braced about and leave it alone for one day — no settling it, no read on what they owe.
cells.core: Running well, this is a table where give and take sort themselves out. You offer what you have, someone answers, and nobody audits it, because the trust does the arithmetic so you don't have to. Right now you're settling a bill nobody has run up yet. Somewhere ahead you've already decided what the other person owes, what you'll put in, how it comes out even, and the balancing runs faster than the actual giving ever could. Holding the exchange together is carrying more than the exchange can hold, and they can feel the pressure before they've said a word. Leaving one trade alone for a day gives back the room to find out what it actually is.

cells.tense: You're standing where a moment has already passed, still treating the level as something you'll get to when it's safer.
cells.ask: Say one sentence of thanks to one person today — no more than that, and no asking for anything back.
cells.core: Working well, you're the one who says the plain thank-you and lets the other person's answer land, and favors move between you and the people around you without anyone counting them. Now the traffic has gone quiet. You put something out less often and take in less, and it looks fine from outside — the table is set, the chairs are full, and almost nothing is passing between them. The fair exchange that's part of how you're made isn't being practised, so it isn't shaping anything right now. Refining it is small: one clear act of giving or thanks, today, and let it land on the other person, which hands back the plain fact of what they do with it.
cells.sheetLine: The exchange has gone quiet, and you can start it again with one plain act.

cells.tense: You're already keeping the exchange level every day, and calling it something that just happens between people.
cells.ask: Name one moment this week where you actually decided what was fair, and say it plainly to yourself — 'that was my call.'
cells.core: Running well, you read what people owe and what's owed to you faster than they do, and a tilted favor gets nudged back without a scene — the bill already split, the awkward favor already returned, the awkwardness absorbed before anyone feels it. That reading is live now, in how you split a check, who you check in on, what you let slide and what you quietly cover. But you explain it as the fairness organizing itself, or as what anyone in your position would do. Your hand is on the scale, and you won't sign for it. Saying one call out loud gives back the plain fact that the fairness was a decision, and yours.
cells.sheetLine: The fairness you're holding happens because you're holding it, and you don't say so.
